MonitoringProgramDescription: The Nearshore Human Health monitoring program collects Escherichia Coli (E. coli) samples to help resource managers ensure Lake Tahoe’s waters remain safe for public recreation. Water quality samples are collected between June and September at many beaches around the lake. More information about the sampling program are available here. A safe to swim map depicting recently collected E. coli data is available here.
MonitoringApproach: Water quality samples for E. coli are taken throughout the summer at popular beaches around Lake Tahoe. E. coli is an indicator of the presence of harmful pathogens or viruses associated with recent contamination by wastewater or other fecal contamination. Individuals who swim in or contact water with elevated levels of E. coli may be at risk of getting sick because of potential exposure to harmful pathogens or viruses associated with wastewater or other fecal contamination.
